title: Problem Atlas
summary: Interactive node-based scenario map allowing users to navigate domain challenges down to AI solutions, process improvements, and requirement blockers. Search the map, follow the edges, and open a node to see what unblocks the next step.
prompt:
# Build Problem Atlas

You are an expert frontend architect. Build a production-ready interactive decision map called "Problem Atlas" and ship it as a static GitHub Pages site.

Live reference: https://clarkngo.github.io/problem-atlas/
Repository: https://github.com/clarkngo/problem-atlas

## Target Architecture & Stack
- Vite, React, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS.
- React Flow for the node canvas, with custom nodes.
- Dagre for automatic top-down layout. Do not hand-place a large graph.
- Fuse.js for fuzzy search across challenges, solutions, and blockers.
- Client-side only. Typed JSON is the database.
- Set Vite base to /problem-atlas/ before you reference any asset.
- Deploy the dist folder with GitHub Actions.

## Product purpose
Problem Atlas lets a person start at a domain challenge and walk downward through process improvements, AI solution options, and the requirement blockers in the way. It should feel like an operational atlas: dense, calm, and fast to scan.

## Key Features & Layout Rules
- The canvas fills the viewport. A slim header carries the title, the active domain, and search.
- Three node types, each visually distinct and readable at the default zoom: Challenge, Solution, and Blocker.
- Edges show direction. A challenge leads to an improvement or a solution. A blocker attaches as a constraint.
- Clicking a node opens a detail panel with the summary, prerequisites, and neighboring nodes. On a phone that panel is a bottom sheet.
- Search highlights matches and frames the first hit. A query with no matches explains itself in the toolbar.
- Include fit-view, zoom, and reset-layout controls.
- Choose one visual material and stay with it. Do not ship the default React Flow demo theme.

## Component Tree
App
  Header
  Toolbar
  AtlasCanvas
    ChallengeNode
    SolutionNode
    BlockerNode
  DetailPanel
  Legend

## Data model
- Node: id, type (challenge | solution | blocker), title, summary, domain, tags, requirements[]
- Edge: id, source, target, relation (leads-to | improves | blocked-by)
- Seed at least two domains. Each challenge reaches both a solution and a blocker.

## Step-by-Step Implementation Strategy
1. Scaffold Vite + React + TypeScript and Tailwind. Set the base path to /problem-atlas/.
2. Define the TypeScript model and a realistic seed file.
3. Build the three custom nodes and a Dagre layout helper that returns ranked positions.
4. Render the graph in React Flow. Fit the view on load.
5. Add Fuse.js search that dims non-matching nodes and focuses the first match.
6. Add the detail panel, legend, domain filter, and mobile bottom sheet.
7. Check keyboard access, contrast, and the phone layout.
8. Add the GitHub Actions workflow that builds and deploys dist to GitHub Pages.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The map lays itself out and stays readable at the default zoom.
- [ ] Search, domain filter, and node details work without a reload.
- [ ] Challenge, solution, and blocker are distinguishable without relying on color alone.
- [ ] The phone layout keeps the canvas usable and moves details into a bottom sheet.
- [ ] The production build loads at /problem-atlas/ with no missing assets.

title: Physical AI & Operational Tech
summary: Interactive educational hub exploring Cyber-Physical Systems, Digital Twins, and Operational Technology automation. Chapters walk from a plain-language concept to how that concept shows up in sensors, control loops, and shop-floor systems.
prompt:
# Build Physical AI & Operational Tech

You are a technical educator and frontend engineer. Build a modern static documentation and lab site called "Physical AI & Operational Tech" for GitHub Pages.

Live reference: https://clarkngo.github.io/physical-ai/
Repository: https://github.com/clarkngo/physical-ai

## Target Architecture & Stack
- Astro with TypeScript and Tailwind CSS.
- Content lives in Markdown or MDX collections, not in one giant page component.
- No backend and no account system.
- Set the Astro base to /physical-ai/.
- Deploy the static build with GitHub Actions.
- Use a client island only if a single widget needs state. Reading must work without it.

## Product purpose
An educational hub for Cyber-Physical Systems, digital twins, and operational technology automation. A reader should move from a plain-language concept to how that concept shows up on a real system: sensors, control loops, twins, and the operational risks around them.

## Key Features & Layout Rules
- Home is a map of the subject: three or four entry paths, not a marketing hero.
- A persistent sidebar lists the chapters. The current page is obvious.
- Each chapter is short, with a definition, a concrete system example, and a note on where it fails.
- Cover cyber-physical systems, digital twins, and operational technology automation.
- Use callouts for definitions, lab notes, and safety or failure warnings.
- Diagrams are designed figures with a caption and a one-sentence reading guide.
- The page column is a comfortable reading measure. Code and tables scroll inside themselves.
- Pick a lab / field-manual visual material. Do not clone a default docs theme and only change the logo.

## Component Tree
BaseLayout
  Header
  Sidebar
  Chapter
    Definition
    Figure
    Callout
    NextPrev
  Home (subject map)

## Step-by-Step Implementation Strategy
1. Scaffold Astro + TypeScript + Tailwind. Set base to /physical-ai/.
2. Define a content collection for chapters: title, summary, order, section, and body.
3. Build the base layout, sidebar, and header. Mark the active chapter.
4. Build the home page as a subject map that links into the collection.
5. Write starter chapters for cyber-physical systems, digital twins, and OT automation. Include one figure and one warning callout in each.
6. Add previous and next links from the collection order.
7. Check the phone layout, contrast, and focus states.
8. Add the GitHub Actions workflow that builds and deploys the static output to GitHub Pages.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A new chapter is added by creating a content file, not by editing a router by hand.
- [ ] Home, sidebar, and chapter pages share one layout.
- [ ] The three core themes include a concrete system example, not only a definition.
- [ ] The site is readable on a phone without horizontal page scroll.
- [ ] The production build loads at /physical-ai/ with no missing assets.

title: Prompt Builder
summary: Interactive tool for composing, parameterizing, and formatting structured system prompts for LLMs. Fill a template's variables, watch the assembled prompt update, and copy it without sending it to a model.
prompt:
# Build Prompt Builder

You are an AI tools engineer. Build a client-side React app called "Prompt Builder" for composing, parameterizing, and formatting structured system prompts. Ship it on GitHub Pages.

Live reference: https://clarkngo.github.io/prompt-builder/
Repository: https://github.com/clarkngo/prompt-builder

## Target Architecture & Stack
- React, TypeScript, Vite, and Tailwind CSS.
- Persist templates in localStorage. No account, no database, and no model API.
- The tool formats a prompt. It does not call an LLM and it never asks for an API key.
- Set Vite base to /prompt-builder/.
- Deploy dist with GitHub Actions.

## Product purpose
A workbench where a system prompt is a template with named variables, not one brittle text blob. The user picks a template, fills the fields, sees the assembled prompt update, and copies it.

## Key Features & Layout Rules
- The first screen is the workbench: template list, variable form, and live assembled prompt.
- A template has a name, a short description, and a body. Variables are written as double-brace tokens and rendered as labeled fields.
- Editing a field updates the assembled prompt immediately. Unfilled tokens stay visible.
- Seed a coding-agent template, a writing-editor template, and a research-brief template.
- Let the user save, duplicate, and delete their own templates. Seed templates can be duplicated, not destroyed.
- Copy puts the assembled prompt on the clipboard and confirms it.
- Parameterize with structured fields. Do not add a control that calls a model.
- Phone layout stacks the form above the preview. Desktop shows them side by side.
- Choose a precise, tool-like visual material. Do not ship a generic chat-app clone.

## Component Tree
App
  Header
  TemplateList
  VariableForm
  PromptPreview
  TemplateEditor
  Toast

## Data model
- Template: id, name, description, body, builtin
- Scan the body for double-brace tokens and render one field per token name.
- Store user templates and the current draft in localStorage under a versioned key.

## Step-by-Step Implementation Strategy
1. Scaffold Vite + React + TypeScript and Tailwind. Set base to /prompt-builder/.
2. Define the template model, the token parser, and the assembler. Cover a missing value, a repeated token, and a body with no tokens.
3. Seed three builtin templates.
4. Build the workbench layout: list, form, and preview.
5. Add save, duplicate, and delete for user templates, with localStorage hydration on load.
6. Add copy with a success and failure message, plus an empty state for a template with no fields.
7. Check the phone stack, the desktop split, keyboard access, and contrast.
8. Add the GitHub Actions workflow that builds and deploys dist to GitHub Pages.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Changing a variable updates the preview immediately.
- [ ] A template with two tokens produces those fields and no others.
- [ ] User templates survive a reload. Builtin templates survive a delete attempt.
- [ ] Copy writes the assembled prompt once every field is filled.
- [ ] The app never requests an API key.
- [ ] The production build loads at /prompt-builder/ with no missing assets.

title: Maritime OT Security
summary: A 12-lesson / 5-day practitioner curriculum for securing ships and port control systems. Course navigation pairs technical material with worked examples, browser sims, and a safeguards-first responsible-use policy.
prompt:
# Build Maritime Operational Technology Security

You are a curriculum designer and frontend engineer. Build a static course site called "Maritime Operational Technology Security" for GitHub Pages.

Live reference: https://clarkngo.github.io/maritime-ot/
Repository: https://github.com/clarkngo/maritime-ot

## Target Architecture & Stack
- Static HTML (or Astro/Vite if you prefer), Tailwind optional, client-side only.
- Set the GitHub Pages base path to /maritime-ot/.
- No backend. Lessons are content files or structured HTML sections.
- Deploy with GitHub Actions.

## Product purpose
A 12-lesson, 5-day practitioner curriculum for anyone who needs to understand and defend the operational technology that keeps ships moving and ports running — bridge, engine room, ballast, cargo, and terminal systems. Each lesson pairs technical material with a worked example, a hands-on activity, and a browser-run simulation.

## Key Features & Layout Rules
- Home is course navigation, not a marketing landing page.
- Lead with a collapsible "Safeguards & Responsible Use" panel: safety outranks the exercise, simulation-only labs, air-gapped segments, defensive scope, scrubbed real-world data, AI-content review, accessible by default.
- Lesson cards show title, one-sentence outcome, and key terms.
- Cover: shipboard OT history → IT/OT principles at sea → field devices → IT protocols → maritime/industrial protocols → threat landscape → countermeasures → IACS/IMO/NIST/IEC frameworks → GRC → access control → monitoring/IR → capstone teachable module.
- Dark mode toggle is fine if it preserves contrast.
- Do not ship working exploit code, live malware samples, or attack procedures against live navigation or control systems.

## Component Tree
CourseShell
  Header (title, course code, instructor, theme)
  SafeguardsPanel
  LessonIndex
    LessonCard
  FrameworksExpandable
  PolicyFooter

## Step-by-Step Implementation Strategy
1. Scaffold the static site with base /maritime-ot/.
2. Define a lesson content model: day, number, title, outcome, keyTerms[], body.
3. Build the shell, safeguards panel, and lesson index.
4. Seed all 12 lessons with accurate maritime OT framing and case-study language (cause/impact/lesson — not attack runbooks).
5. Add frameworks expandable and the full safeguards policy page/section.
6. Check keyboard access, contrast, and phone layout.
7. Deploy dist (or site root) to GitHub Pages.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Safeguards are visible before labs.
- [ ] All 12 lessons are reachable from the index.
- [ ] Content stays defensive and simulation-scoped.
- [ ] Production build loads at /maritime-ot/.

title: Courses Catalog
summary: A multi-course catalog of practical short courses on AI, applied systems, and modern tech — built for beginners, organized by category, with Available vs Coming soon states and deep links into individual curricula.
prompt:
# Build Courses Catalog

You are an education-product engineer. Build a static Astro course catalog called "Courses" for GitHub Pages.

Live reference: https://clarkngo.github.io/courses/
Repository: https://github.com/clarkngo/courses

## Target Architecture & Stack
- Astro, MDX, TypeScript, and Tailwind.
- Course and lesson content live in collections, not hard-coded route lists.
- Set Astro base to /courses/.
- Client-side only for browsing. Deploy with GitHub Actions.

## Product purpose
A catalog of practical short courses on AI, modern technology, and applied systems — built for complete beginners and taught through real-world projects. Home shows every course across categories with clear Available / Coming soon states.

## Key Features & Layout Rules
- Hero states the audience and the promise in one short block.
- Category sections group courses (AI & Machine Learning, etc.).
- Each course card: title, short description, lesson count, status badge, link into the course.
- Available courses are clickable; coming-soon courses look intentional, not broken.
- Course pages use a consistent chapter/lesson layout with progress-friendly navigation.
- One visual material for the whole catalog. Do not invent a second design system per course.

## Component Tree
BaseLayout
  Header
  Home
    CategorySection
      CourseCard
  CourseLayout
    LessonNav
    LessonContent

## Step-by-Step Implementation Strategy
1. Scaffold Astro + MDX + Tailwind. Set base to /courses/.
2. Define collections for courses and lessons (title, category, status, summary, order, body).
3. Build the catalog home from the collection.
4. Build the course and lesson templates.
5. Seed several Available courses and at least one Coming soon entry.
6. Check phone layout, empty states, and focus order.
7. Deploy to GitHub Pages.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Adding a course is a content-file change, not a router edit.
- [ ] Available vs Coming soon is obvious.
- [ ] Catalog and course pages share one visual system.
- [ ] Production build loads at /courses/.

title: ScriptedOT
summary: Cinematic anchors for OT/ICS security engineering: film and TV scenes become four-panel comics that introduce cyber-physical concepts, then ground them in documented incidents, ISA/IEC 62443 / NIST SP 800-82, and engineering runbooks.
prompt:
# Build ScriptedOT

You are a technical educator and frontend engineer. Build a static site called "ScriptedOT" for GitHub Pages.

Live reference: https://clarkngo.github.io/scripted-ot/
Repository: https://github.com/clarkngo/scripted-ot

## Target Architecture & Stack
- Static HTML/CSS/JS or Astro + Tailwind. Client-side only.
- Set base path to /scripted-ot/.
- Module content can be JSON/MD; comics are image assets with captions.
- Deploy with GitHub Actions.

## Product purpose
Use recognizable dramatic scenes from film and television to introduce complex cyber-physical / OT-ICS concepts, then ground each module in a documented industrial incident, ISA/IEC 62443 and NIST SP 800-82, and a reproducible engineering runbook.

## Key Features & Layout Rules
- Every module follows the same four-part structure:
  1) Cinematic Anchor (four-panel comic + dialogue + character→role mapping)
  2) ICS Architecture (Purdue levels, protocols, control logic)
  3) Empirical Grounding (real-incident comic, case, cinematic-vs-reality matrix, root cause)
  4) Runbook / Countermeasures (telemetry envelopes, mitigation steps, standard clauses)
- Home lists ~10 modules across domains (nuclear, power, water, building automation, oil & gas, aerospace, maritime defense, traffic, healthcare facilities) with Live status.
- Fiction is a teaching hook. The empirical section must stay factual and defensive.
- Comics need captions and alt text. Do not rely on the image alone.

## Component Tree
AppShell
  Header
  HowItWorks
  ModuleGrid
    ModuleCard
  ModulePage
    ComicStrip
    ArchitectureBlock
    GroundingBlock
    RunbookBlock

## Step-by-Step Implementation Strategy
1. Scaffold the static site with base /scripted-ot/.
2. Define the module content model and seed at least two complete modules.
3. Build home grid + module page template matching the four-part structure.
4. Add comic strip component with alt text and panel labels.
5. Finish remaining modules or leave Coming soon placeholders intentionally.
6. Accessibility and phone pass, then deploy to GitHub Pages.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Every live module exposes all four sections.
- [ ] Cinematic vs reality is explicit, not blurred.
- [ ] Comics are keyboard-reachable and described.
- [ ] Production build loads at /scripted-ot/.

title: CityU Guides
summary: CityU Guides ebook library: browse practical guides, optionally complete a short Google Form, then unlock downloads on the page. Use the card flip toggle for a gated lead-capture prompt or an open, ungated library prompt.
prompt:
# Build CityU Guides (gated ebook library)

You are a frontend engineer. Build a static GitHub Pages ebook library called "CityU Guides".

Live reference: https://clarkngo.github.io/cityu-ebooks/
Repository: https://github.com/clarkngo/cityu-ebooks

## Target Architecture & Stack
- Static site (HTML/CSS/JS or the repo's site/ folder conventions).
- Base path /cityu-ebooks/.
- Lead capture via an embedded Google Form. No custom backend.
- Deploy with GitHub Actions.

## Product purpose
Practical free guides for students, partners, and career changers. Browse the library, complete a short form, then unlock the download on the same page.

## Key Features & Layout Rules
- Library grid of guides (cover, title, short blurb).
- Flow: Choose a guide → Share a few details (embedded Google Form) → Download unlocks on this page.
- No account system. Instant unlock after form submit (postMessage, thank-you redirect param, or equivalent client pattern).
- Clear empty and loading states for the unlock step.
- Brand as City University of Seattle materials without looking like a generic lead-gen template.
- Accessible form and download controls.

## Component Tree
LibraryPage
  Header
  HowItWorks
  GuideGrid
    GuideCard
  GateModal or GatePanel
    EmbeddedForm
    DownloadUnlock

## Step-by-Step Implementation Strategy
1. Scaffold / reuse site/ with base /cityu-ebooks/.
2. Define guide metadata and file assets.
3. Build grid + how-it-works.
4. Embed Google Form and wire unlock UX after submit.
5. Test keyboard path and phone layout.
6. Deploy to GitHub Pages.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Guides list without an account.
- [ ] Download stays locked until the gate completes.
- [ ] Unlock happens on-page after submit.
- [ ] Production build loads at /cityu-ebooks/.

title: Project Ouroboros
summary: A long-form business and engineering novel about runaway AI promises, invisible debt, and the architecture of survival. Manuscript in Markdown, built with Pandoc/Make into HTML/PDF/EPUB and published to GitHub Pages.
prompt:
# Build Project Ouroboros (reading site)

You are a technical writer and publishing engineer. Build a GitHub Pages reading experience for the novel "Project Ouroboros" from a Pandoc manuscript pipeline.

Repository: https://github.com/clarkngo/project-ouroboros

## Target Architecture & Stack
- Source of truth: manuscript Markdown chapters under act folders (chNN-slug.md, lexical order).
- Makefile + Pandoc for html / pdf / epub / site outputs.
- GitHub Actions publish.yml builds the site on push to main.
- CSS in templates/manuscript.css. Metadata in templates/metadata.yaml.
- docs/ holds character bible, system architecture, and glossary.

## Product purpose
Publish a long-form business/engineering novel about a company selling "autonomous operations" multi-agent LLM systems — and the gap between that promise and disciplined, deterministic engineering. No speculative AI powers; tension comes from skipped engineering under growth pressure.

## Key Features & Layout Rules
- Reading site is calm typography for long sessions: measure, leading, chapter navigation.
- Front matter + three acts (The Mandate, The Swamp, The Architecture of Survival), ~24 chapters.
- Optional sticky chapter nav and progress indicator.
- Link out to characters / glossary docs without breaking the reading flow.
- Do not turn the novel into a marketing landing page.

## Component / Artifact Tree
manuscript/act-0N/chNN-*.md
templates/metadata.yaml
templates/manuscript.css
docs/characters.md
docs/system-architecture.md
docs/technical-glossary.md
Makefile
.github/workflows/publish.yml
site/ (Pages output)

## Step-by-Step Implementation Strategy
1. Confirm Pandoc toolchain and Makefile targets (html, pdf, epub, site, clean).
2. Style the HTML build for long-form reading.
3. Wire GitHub Actions to build site/ and deploy to Pages.
4. Verify chapter order and navigation.
5. Proof on phone and desktop.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] make html and make site succeed locally.
- [ ] Push to main publishes a readable Pages site.
- [ ] Chapters appear in act order.
- [ ] Typography stays readable for long sessions.

title: Maritime Atlas — Illustrations
summary: A single-page illustrations & photos gallery inside Maritime Atlas: raster visuals (AI illustrations and licensed photos) filtered by topic, reviewed before publish, with attribution and model credits in a lightbox. Schematics live elsewhere — this page is only the raster gallery.
prompt:
# Build Page: Maritime Atlas Illustrations & Photos

You are a frontend engineer. Build ONE page — not the whole Maritime Atlas site — for GitHub Pages:

Live page: https://clarkngo.github.io/maritime-atlas/illustrations.html
Repository: https://github.com/clarkngo/maritime-atlas

## Scope (page blueprint)
- Deliver illustrations.html (or the equivalent route) as a focused gallery page.
- Reuse the atlas shell/header if it already exists; do not redesign the entire site.
- Schematics (author SVG diagrams) stay on category pages. This page is raster only.

## Target Architecture & Stack
- Match the existing Maritime Atlas stack (static HTML/JS or the repo's current tooling).
- Base path /maritime-atlas/. Asset URLs must work under that base.
- Client-side filter/tag UI. No backend.

## Product purpose
Present AI-generated illustrations and licensed photographs in the same topic categories as schematics, but tagged, filtered, and attributed separately. Every image is human-reviewed; generation tools and models are credited in the lightbox.

## Key Features & Layout Rules
- Page title: Illustrations & Photos under the Maritime Atlas brand.
- Intro copy states raster vs schematic split and the review-before-publication rule.
- Filter chips by topic/tag. Empty state when a filter yields nothing.
- Grid of thumbnails; click opens a lightbox with caption, attribution, model/tool credit, and review status.
- Show a clear "Review before publication" callout for unpublished / pending items.
- Accessible: keyboard lightbox, focus trap, alt text required.
- Do not auto-publish unreviwed AI images.

## Component Tree (this page)
AtlasShell (existing)
  IllustrationsPage
    Intro
    ReviewCallout
    TagFilters
    ImageGrid
      Thumbnail
    Lightbox
      Attribution
      ModelCredits

## Step-by-Step Implementation Strategy
1. Add the page route/file under the existing atlas project.
2. Define an image content model: id, title, topic tags, src, alt, attribution, tool/model, reviewed.
3. Build filter + grid + lightbox with keyboard support.
4. Seed a few reviewed examples and one pending state for the callout.
5. Verify under /maritime-atlas/illustrations.html on phone and desktop.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Page loads at /maritime-atlas/illustrations.html.
- [ ] Filters and lightbox work without a full-site rewrite.
- [ ] Attribution and model credits are visible per image.
- [ ] Unreviewed items cannot look "published" by accident.
